76723.body:

Автор: Financial Times


Автор: Financial Times

Hello from the FT newsroom, where we are closely following the sell-off of tech equities.  Investor concerns about AI overspending have rocked semiconductor stocks, hitting Asian markets particularly hard. South Korean chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics tumbled on Tuesday, while a rout in US chip and memory stocks temporarily dragged the Nasdaq 100 into correction territory. Anxieties about the levels of financing and regulation were intensified following proposals for the US administration to restrict Chinese AI models. In an interview with the FT, Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg said this would not be “an effective solution”, contrary to the stances of the bosses of Anthropic and OpenAI.  Meanwhile, the UK market has benefited from its low exposure to tech, with the FTSE 100 reaching a record high in early trading yesterday. Its skew towards energy and finance had proved a useful means of diversification, analysts said, with Barclays’ head of European equity strategy labelling it an “almost anti-tech index”.  My choices this week As firefighters in France and Spain struggle to contain wildfire outbreaks, Australia offers some useful lessons on proactive prevention. Early warning systems, firebreaks and lowering household risks can help “put the fires out five years before they start”. (Free to read) Kyiv is changing its tactics to force Russian refineries offline for longer to increase the costs of the war for Moscow, the FT’s Ukraine correspondent Christopher Miller explains. The levels of uranium contained in cobalt exported by the Democratic Republic of Congo between 2000 and 2024 were enough to create 600 nuclear weapons, new research suggests. An FT and Lighthouse Reports investigation sheds light on the murky practice. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has suggested he is open to raising taxes to fund extensive social care reform, adding that he is prepared to use his “political capital” to tackle the issue. On Tuesday, the FT revealed that Fifa plans to sell a stake in a new $20bn commercial entity. The proposal has been met with a backlash from Europe and North America’s football governing bodies. The FT is covering the outlook of the United Arab Emirates in a five-part series spanning the country’s geopolitical and corporate ambitions. 🧠 Crypto News Brief: Markets held their breath as a hawkish Fed pause pinned Bitcoin near $64K and left Ether sliding. Fresh hacks and a stalling CLARITY Act kept sentiment in fear — even as Wall Street and travel giants deepened crypto adoption. 🏦 Hawkish Fed Hold Pins Bitcoin Near $64K The FOMC held rates at 3.50–3.75% in a rare 9-3 vote on July 29, with three regional presidents dissenting toward a hike — the first triple hawkish split since 2016. Bitcoin briefly touched $64,700 before fading to around $64,000, as roughly $300 million in leveraged positions were liquidated across tens of thousands of traders. Read full story → 📊 Bitcoin ETFs Flip Green as Ether Funds Bleed US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $32.1 million in net inflows on July 29, snapping a four-day outflow streak, led by BlackRock's IBIT at $89.8 million. Spot Ether ETFs slipped into net outflows on the same day, underscoring a capital rotation back toward Bitcoin and Ethereum's fading market dominance. More details → 🏛️ CLARITY Act Stalls as Senate Misses Recess Deadline Prediction-market odds on the CLARITY Act passing crashed to around 28% after the Senate missed its August-recess deadline, leaving the crypto market-structure bill in limbo. Prolonged gridlock could push the SEC to write securities-side rules on its own while lawmakers keep debating how to split oversight with the CFTC. Read more → 🔓 Ostium Post-Mortem Confirms $23.75M Off-Chain Breach Arbitrum perpetuals exchange Ostium published its post-mortem confirming attackers drained $23.75 million in USDC from its liquidity vault via a compromised off-chain oracle signer — not a smart-contract flaw. Trader collateral was untouched, trading resumed July 23, and a recovery plan for liquidity providers is being finalized. See details → ⚠️ Senator Lummis' X Account Hacked to Push Scam Token Hackers briefly seized Senator Cynthia Lummis' verified X account on July 29, posting a fake "$USA Token" Solana meme coin through a pump.fun link before the messages were deleted within minutes. Lummis is the Senate's most vocal CLARITY Act advocate, making the timing of the takeover especially pointed. Read full story → 💼 Morgan Stanley Launches Staked Ether and Solana ETPs Morgan Stanley Investment Management listed staked Ethereum (MSSE) and Solana (MSOL) exchange-traded products on NYSE Arca, each charging 0.14% and passing staking
